title: INF GSD Limited Edition — Infinity Group Measurement System
description: Single canonical measurement contract for the Infinity Group. Merges the GSD layered spec (v1.0), the Hermes business-measurement-system schema (v1.0.0), and the existing Sales & Marketing Funnel Tracker model. This file supersedes both predecessors. Any AI, agent or system reading, writing or reporting on portfolio metrics reads this and nothing else.

supersedes.kept: layer architecture, named owners, structured RAG thresholds, leading/lagging typing, operating cadence, 1-3-1 escalation, band targets, DDA governance note
brand focus_metrics matrix, framework_pillar tagging, severity-based alerting, data_sources map, implementation phase tracking, metric-library-not-duplicated approach

structural_rules: Every metric has exactly one named human owner. Never a department.
Metrics are defined ONCE in the library and referenced by brands. No duplication per brand.
Layer 1 is capped at 12. A thirteenth requires a deletion.
Targets are structured objects, never strings. Agents must be able to evaluate them without parsing English.
Impact metrics never excuse financial reds; financial greens never excuse impact reds.
Two consecutive reds trigger a playbook review, not a performance conversation.

pillars.name: Dan Martell — Buy Back Your Time
pillars.principle: Time is the only non-renewable resource. Move hours into high-value work and systemise the rest.

pillars.name: Simon Squibb — Help First / Give Without Take
pillars.principle: Help people first, money follows. Commercial success is a byproduct of value genuinely delivered.

brands.name: Papa Pasta
brands.note: In the Funnel Tracker as an FND product but absent from both predecessor schemas. See reconciliation_gaps.

brands.name: ACDC Express
brands.note: In the Funnel Tracker as an FND product but absent from both predecessor schemas.

products.note: The Funnel Tracker measures nine PRODUCTS. The measurement system measures BRANDS. These are different granularities and do not map one-to-one. Every product must resolve to a brand for roll-up.
products.unmapped_note: Divorced Dads has no funnel tracker product. It needs either a tenth funnel tab or an explicit exemption on record.

funnel_model.description: The Sales & Marketing Funnel Tracker model, wired into the measurement system as the sales engine. Previously absent from both predecessor schemas.
funnel_model.source_workbook: Sales & Marketing Funnel Tracker (Zoho Sheet, 15 tabs)

fnd.note: FND products are NEVER measured in Rand at funnel level. Locations sold is the output. Rand follows later via ops.unit_margin.

source_level_attribution.reason: Explicitly descoped at funnel tracker design stage

cycle_time_tracking.reason: Explicitly descoped at funnel tracker design stage. NOTE: the v1 spec re-introduced sal.cycle_length in breach of this decision; removed in v2.0 pending an explicit reversal.

metrics.name: Revenue (month)
metrics.definition: Monthly revenue booked, per brand.

metrics.name: Gross Margin
metrics.definition: (Revenue − COGS) / Revenue.
metrics.correction_note: Hermes v1 applied a flat >=60% group-wide. A farm and a franchisor cannot carry software margins; a single target would show permanent red on TLF and ACDC and permanent green on nothing useful.

metrics.name: Net Burn
metrics.definition: Monthly net cash outflow.

metrics.name: Runway
metrics.definition: Cash balance divided by monthly net burn.

metrics.name: Debtor Days
metrics.definition: Average days to collect receivables.

metrics.name: Opex as % of Revenue
metrics.definition: Operating expenditure as a share of revenue.

metrics.name: Recurring Revenue Ratio
metrics.definition: Recurring revenue as a share of total revenue.

metrics.name: LTV:CAC Ratio
metrics.definition: Lifetime value divided by customer acquisition cost.

metrics.name: CAC Payback Period
metrics.definition: CAC divided by monthly gross margin per customer.

metrics.name: Revenue vs Plan
metrics.definition: Month-to-date actual revenue divided by month-to-date budget, all brands.

metrics.name: Headcount
metrics.definition: Staff per brand, FTE.

metrics.name: Revenue per FTE
metrics.definition: Trailing twelve-month revenue divided by FTE headcount.

metrics.name: Voluntary Attrition (12m)
metrics.definition: Voluntary leavers as a share of average headcount over twelve months.

metrics.name: 90-Day New Hire Success
metrics.definition: New hires still employed and meeting expectations at ninety days.
metrics.note: Below 85% the cause is almost always hiring on interviews rather than paid trial work.

metrics.name: Team Satisfaction
metrics.definition: Employee satisfaction survey score, 1-10.

metrics.name: Training Hours
metrics.definition: Training hours per person per month.

metrics.name: Playbook Coverage
metrics.definition: Roles with a current documented playbook divided by total roles.

metrics.name: System Uptime
metrics.definition: Availability of production systems.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Resolve (P1)
metrics.definition: Average hours to resolve priority-one incidents.

metrics.name: Open Tickets
metrics.definition: Support ticket backlog size.

metrics.name: Automation Coverage
metrics.definition: Automated processes divided by total repeatable processes.

metrics.name: AI Adoption
metrics.definition: Share of team actively using AI tools in their workflow.

metrics.name: MFA Coverage
metrics.definition: Accounts with multi-factor authentication enforced.

metrics.name: Codebase Health Score
metrics.definition: Codebase health rated 1-10 where 10 is clean.
metrics.correction_note: Hermes v1 defined 10 = clean but set target '< 5', which targets a broken codebase. Renamed and inverted so direction and target agree.

metrics.name: Marketing Spend
metrics.definition: Total marketing spend in the period, per product.

metrics.name: Cost per Lead
metrics.definition: Marketing spend divided by leads generated.

metrics.name: Marketing ROI
metrics.definition: Output value attributable to marketing divided by marketing spend.

metrics.name: Brand Reach
metrics.definition: Total audience size across owned channels.

metrics.name: Help-First Content
metrics.definition: Free value pieces published with no gate and no catch.

metrics.name: Community Size
metrics.definition: Followers, members and engaged community across channels.

metrics.name: Pipeline Value
metrics.definition: Total value of open deals.

metrics.name: Pipeline Coverage
metrics.definition: Weighted open pipeline divided by next-period target.

metrics.name: Deals Won
metrics.definition: Closed-won deals in the period.

metrics.name: Win Rate
metrics.definition: Deals won divided by deals closed.

metrics.name: Average Deal Size
metrics.definition: Won value divided by won count.

metrics.name: Net Revenue Retention
metrics.definition: Revenue retained plus expanded from existing customers, over opening revenue.

metrics.name: Churn
metrics.definition: Customers lost divided by total customers.

metrics.name: Production Output
metrics.definition: Units or kilograms produced. TLF: mushrooms, microgreens.

metrics.name: Quality Score
metrics.definition: Product or service quality rating, 1-10.

metrics.name: On-Time Delivery
metrics.definition: Deliveries on time divided by total deliveries.

metrics.name: Customer Satisfaction
metrics.definition: Customer satisfaction rating, 1-10.

metrics.name: Margin per Unit / Site
metrics.definition: Gross margin generated per operating unit or franchise site.
metrics.note: This is where FND revenue is actually measured. The funnel measures locations sold; this measures what each location earns.

metrics.name: SOP / Audit Compliance
metrics.definition: Score achieved on the standard operating audit.

metrics.name: Buyback Rate
metrics.definition: Ricardo's effective hourly rate divided by four. The Rand threshold below which a task should be delegated rather than done.
metrics.correction_note: Hermes v1 defined buyback_rate as 'HVA time / total work time' with a 50% target. That is Martell's Production-quadrant measure, not the Buyback Rate. The Buyback Rate is a currency-per-hour delegation threshold. Both are useful; they are now separate metrics and correctly named.

metrics.name: High-Value Activity Time
metrics.definition: Share of working hours spent in the Production quadrant of the DRIP matrix.

metrics.name: Delegation Ratio
metrics.definition: Tasks delegated divided by tasks owned.

metrics.name: Decisions Escalated to CEO
metrics.definition: Count of decisions in the week that could not be closed without Ricardo.
metrics.note: The most diagnostic number in the system. Rising means the business is becoming a job rather than an asset.

metrics.name: Eliminated Tasks
metrics.definition: Low-value tasks removed from workflows entirely.

metrics.name: Replacement Ladder Position
metrics.definition: Highest filled rung of the Replacement Ladder, per brand, scored 0-5.

metrics.name: People Helped
metrics.definition: Cumulative people positively impacted — customers, franchisees, employees, community.

metrics.name: Purpose Score
metrics.definition: Clarity and strength of brand mission, 1-10. Scored by whether the team can state the Dream unprompted.

metrics.name: Jobs Sustained
metrics.definition: Total FTE plus franchise-level employment supported by the group.

metrics.name: Leads Generated
metrics.definition: New leads generated in the month, per product. Stage 1 output.

metrics.name: Conversion — Lead to Opportunity
metrics.definition: Leads converted to qualified opportunities. This is the SDR team's number.

metrics.name: Qualified Opportunities
metrics.definition: Leads qualified into opportunities. Stage 2 output.

metrics.name: Cost per Opportunity
metrics.definition: Marketing spend divided by qualified opportunities produced.

metrics.name: Conversion — Opportunity to Close
metrics.definition: Opportunities converted to closed business. This is the Dealmaker team's number.

metrics.name: Funnel Output — Value
metrics.definition: Closed business value. Applies to professional services product lines only.

metrics.name: Funnel Output — Locations Sold
metrics.definition: Franchise locations sold. Applies to FND product lines only. Never expressed in Rand at funnel level.

metrics.name: Key-Person Dependency
metrics.definition: Count of critical functions where the answer to 'if the person running this quit tomorrow, who does the job fall on?' is the owner. The Bottleneck Question — Codie Sanchez framework.
metrics.formula: count(critical_functions where owner is the fallback)
metrics.note: Codie Sanchez — Own or Be Owned. The Bottleneck Question: what system needs to exist so it doesn't matter who leaves?

metrics.name: Cash-on-Cash Return
metrics.definition: Annual cash profit divided by cash invested. The return the owner's actual money earns — Codie Sanchez's primary deal evaluation metric.
metrics.note: Codie Sanchez — boring business benchmark: 30-50%+ cash-on-cash in stabilized years.

metrics.name: Deals Sourced
metrics.definition: Acquisition opportunities sourced in the period — from brokers, direct outreach, media, or network.

metrics.name: Deals in Diligence
metrics.definition: Deals currently in due diligence — actively being evaluated for purchase.

metrics.name: Deals Closed
metrics.definition: Acquisitions completed in the period.

metrics.name: Seller Financing %
metrics.definition: Share of acquisition purchase price financed by the seller — reduces cash outlay and aligns seller incentives.
metrics.note: Codie Sanchez — seller financing is the leverage that makes deals work with less cash down.

ceo_twelve.description: Layer 1. Ricardo's only screen. Twenty minutes, Monday morning. References into the metric library — no separate definitions.
ceo_twelve.note: funnel.output_locations surfaces alongside funnel.output_zar for FND brands; it does not consume a separate slot.

data_sources.zoho_books: Finance — revenue, margin, burn, runway, spend
data_sources.zoho_crm: Sales — pipeline, deals, CAC, LTV, NRR, churn
data_sources.funnel_tracker: Funnel — leads, conversions, opportunities, output. Zoho Sheet workbook, 15 tabs, manual until CRM integration lands.
data_sources.manual_capture: Buyback, delegation, automation, AI adoption, purpose, people helped

alerting.principle: Alert on red flips only. Never send green confirmations — they train people to ignore the channel.

rules.note: Isolates the SDR stage — tells you the bottleneck is qualification, not lead volume
Bottleneck Question — more than 2 critical functions fall back to the owner
Deal flow drying up — buy don't build

cadence.output: Cash, prior-day sales per brand, red flips
Brand boards plus funnel by stage. 1-3-1 on every red.
Full P&L, department boards, playbook audit, impact metrics
Capital reallocation, DRIP audit, ladder rescore, funnel target reset
Preloaded year, purpose review per brand, targets set

rule_1_3_1.description: Any red metric brought to a review arrives as one problem statement, three viable options, one recommendation from the owner.

ladder.action: Owner logs cause in Coda. No meeting time spent.
1-3-1 at the weekly. Action assigned with owner and date.
Playbook review. Person, process or target problem? Assume process first.
Escalate to Quarterly Reset as a capital or structural question.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Funnel is three stages; both schemas modelled one
reconciliation_gaps.detail: Hermes had a single lead_conversion (Leads → Customers, target 8%). the v1 spec had win_rate only. The Funnel Tracker splits conversion across Marketing → SDR → Dealmaker. Collapsing to one number makes it impossible to tell which team is the bottleneck, which is the entire purpose of the tracker.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Added funnel.conv_lead_to_opp (SDR) and funnel.conv_opp_to_close (Dealmaker) as separate metrics with team attribution. Single-stage lead_conversion removed.

reconciliation_gaps.title: FND output unit mismatch
reconciliation_gaps.detail: The Funnel Tracker measures FND products in franchise locations sold, never Rand. Both schemas expressed all sales output in ZAR (deals_won, revenue), which would silently convert locations into money at funnel level and corrupt comparisons.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Split into funnel.output_zar (professional services) and funnel.output_locations (FND), each with applies_to_lines guards. FND Rand is captured downstream at ops.unit_margin.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Brand list does not cover the product list
reconciliation_gaps.detail: The Funnel Tracker runs nine products. Hermes and the v1 spec both listed five brands. Papa Pasta, ACDC Express, INF Consultancy and the three SLA products had no home. Divorced Dads has no funnel product.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Added a products taxonomy with explicit product → brand mapping. Papa Pasta and ACDC Express added as proposed brands. Divorced Dads flagged as unmapped, needing a funnel tab or a recorded exemption.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Marketing cost measured only as blended CAC
reconciliation_gaps.detail: The Funnel Tracker carries cost-per metrics at each stage. Hermes had CAC only, at month and brand grain, sitting under Finance.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Added mkt.cost_per_lead, funnel.cost_per_opportunity and mkt.marketing_roi at product grain under Marketing.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Cycle time re-introduced against a prior scoping decision
reconciliation_gaps.detail: sal.cycle_length appeared in v1.0 despite cycle time being explicitly descoped when the Funnel Tracker was designed.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Removed. Recorded in funnel_model.scope_decisions_carried_forward so it does not creep back in silently.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Buyback Rate was defined as something else
reconciliation_gaps.detail: Hermes defined buyback_rate as HVA time over total work time with a 50% target. That is Martell's Production-quadrant measure. The Buyback Rate is a currency-per-hour delegation threshold: (income ÷ hours) ÷ 4.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Split into founder.buyback_rate (ZAR/hour) and founder.production_pct (percent, target 50). Both retained, correctly named.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Flat 60% gross margin target across the portfolio
reconciliation_gaps.detail: A farm, a franchisor and a SaaS product cannot share a margin target. TLF and ACDC would show permanent red regardless of performance.

reconciliation_gaps.title: Tech debt target contradicted its own scale
reconciliation_gaps.detail: Defined as 1-10 where 10 = clean, then targeted '< 5' — i.e. targeting a broken codebase.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Renamed to Codebase Health Score, direction set higher_is_better, target 7.

reconciliation_gaps.title: No metric had an owner
reconciliation_gaps.detail: Hermes had no owner field at all. the v1 spec had the field but every value was TBC.
reconciliation_gaps.resolution: Field retained and required. Still TBC — this is the Phase 1 blocker and cannot be solved by a schema.

implementation_phases.name: Name an owner for each of the CEO Twelve
Resolve product-to-brand mapping (Papa Pasta, ACDC, Divorced Dads)
Wire Zoho data via Zoho MCP + Google Workspace OAuth
Funnel Tracker feeds funnel.* metrics (manual, then CRM)

open_decisions.question: Papa Pasta and ACDC Express are Funnel Tracker products with no brand board. Promote to full brands, or report inside Infinity Brands?
Divorced Dads has no funnel product. Add a tenth funnel tab, or record an explicit exemption?
INF Consultancy and the three SLA products currently roll into Infinity Brands. Correct, or do they need their own board?
Per-brand gross margin targets are estimates. Confirm or replace with plan figures.
Named owners for all twelve Layer 1 metrics. The system does not function with 'Finance' as an owner.
Reinstate cycle time tracking, or keep it descoped as originally decided?
CEO Twelve now carries 14 Layer 1 metrics (added ops.key_person_dependency + fin.cash_on_cash). Contract caps Layer 1 at 12. Ratify the 14, or demote two to Layer 2?

reading_schema.description: Definitions are static; readings are time-series. Store separately. Funnel readings carry a product_id; all others carry a brand_id.

counts.funnel_metrics_nested_in: mkt and sal — funnel.* metrics carry funnel_stage and team fields
counts.reduction_from_v1: 101 → 59, achieved by defining metrics once in a library and referencing them per brand rather than duplicating
